newsitem.title: Australia: CRICKET-CHAPPELL CALLS FOR TAYLOR'S SCALP.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-CHAPPELL CALLS FOR TAYLOR'S SCALP.

text.p: Out-of-form opener Mark Taylor has run out of time to save himself as Australia captain and should be sacked before next week's first Ashes test against England, former skipper Ian Chappell said on Wednesday.
Chappell called for Taylor's axing after the left-handed opener's latest batting failure on tour, a fourth-ball duck in the penultimate match before the first test begins at Edgbaston on June 5.
"I have not seen anything in Mark Taylor's batting to say he's coming out of the slump," Chappell was quoted as saying in Sydney's Daily Telegraph newspaper.
"(Australia) have got to get two openers in form and I don't think they have got time to mess around with him any more.
"You have really got to ask yourself now: is it a prolonged slump or is he gone?" said Chappell, who is working as a television commentator during the tour.
Chappell's comments came after an anti-Taylor barrage in Australian newspapers on Wednesday.
"Dead Duck" said a Daily Telegraph headline after Taylor's dismissal for nought on Tuesday in the first innings of a three-day match against Gloucestershire.

"Given the Australians' collective poor form so far, there is a strong argument they cannot afford to carry anyone into the test who is so painfully unable to make a decent contribution, regardless of his status as captain," the paper said.
The Sydney Morning Herald agreed that Taylor, who has not scored a test 50 since late 1995 and scored only 18 in the firt two one-day matches against England, should go.
"On top of all that has preceded it (Taylor's latest failure), it is hard to argue that his place is sustainable any longer," the newspaper wrote.
Taylor's immediate future rests with a three-man tour selection panel comprising coach Geoff Marsh, himself as captain and vice-captain Steve Waugh.
